subject: Request: one-time acceleration credit to close Lumen Therapeutics deal
messages:
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Subject: Request: one-time acceleration credit to close Lumen Therapeutics deal

Hi Marissa / Karthik —

Quick context: Lumen Therapeutics (clinical analytics) is on our Q3 board to sign a 3-yr Dedicated + Private package (~$1.45M ARR first year) but legal/procurement is asking for faster signature incentives. They are willing to sign this week if we provide a modest upfront credit that covers an initial onboarding burst and a small consumption buffer.

Why I think this is reasonable:
- High strategic value: they’re evaluating Dedicated for a 3-region rollout in 2027; strong reference potential in oncology analytics.
- Likely expansion: Sales forecast shows 2–3x expansion probability in 12 months if pilot goes well.
- Close velocity: procurement indicated signature within 72 hours if we commit to a small credit + accelerated onboarding calendar.

Proposal (one-time):
- $80k credit applied to first invoice (consumption/onboarding offset).
- Conditional: credit recouped pro rata if churn/termination in first 6 months (clawback clause).
- Term sheet redline attached (redline_term_sheet.pdf) with proposed clawback language.

Attachment: deal_summary.pdf (deal economics & forecast), redline_term_sheet.pdf

Requested ask: Can Finance sign off on this one-time credit (VP/CFO approval) or propose a maximum we must not exceed? I can also offer a mitigant: reduce credit to $50k + a 90-day committed usage minimum if that helps margin.

I need an internal yes/no by EOD so I can keep the procurement window open.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Request: one-time acceleration credit to close Lumen Therapeutics deal

Sofia —

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick questions before I escalate:
1) Net margin impact: can you confirm the 12-month revenue profile and expected token consumption for year 1 as detailed in deal_summary.pdf? I want to run a sensitivity on margin and breakeven.
2) Clawback mechanics: the redline looks ok; legal needs specific language for precise recoupment timing and triggers. If Legal signs off we can make it conditional.
3) Alternative mitigant: you mentioned $50k + 90-day committed usage — what does that look like in unit terms?

If you can respond inline with numbers I’ll prep a brief memo for VP/CFO approval. If we need an executive override, I’ll loop in Jonas.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance (Interim CFO) | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Subject: Re: Request: one-time acceleration credit to close Lumen Therapeutics deal

Marissa / Sofia —

Numbers from the sales forecast and product ops:
- Year 1 committed ARR: $1,450,000 (combo Dedicated + Private).
- Expected onboarding burst (first 60 days): ~1.1M tokens per day for initial verification and model tuning; estimated consumption cost (marginal infra + token cost equivalent) ~ $60k over first 60 days.
- Normalized monthly consumption after ramp: ~160k tokens/day (>$250k/month revenue expectation).

If we do a $80k credit it approximately offsets the onboarding consumption + a small margin for initial support hours. Margin sensitivity: at $80k one-time credit, the 12-month gross margin reduces by ~4.8% on year 1; at $50k that impact is ~3.0%.

Mitigants I suggest:
- $50k credit + 90-day committed usage floor (commitment defined in tokens or $) — reduces immediate hit and still keeps close velocity.
- Shorten credit payback: if they expand >$500k ARR within 12 months, we convert remaining credit into reserved capacity credit (non-cash), protecting cash flow.

I recommend we avoid $80k unless Finance approves; $50k + 90-day floor is likely a good middle ground.

Karthik
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Fwd: Request: one-time acceleration credit to close Lumen Therapeutics deal — VP/CFO approval requested

Jonas —

Forwarding the thread and attachments. We’ve pulled the numbers and Legal is comfortable with the clawback structure as long as Finance signs off on the cap. Karthik recommends $50k + a 90-day committed usage floor as the preferred mitigant; I highlighted the $80k ask as the ask from procurement to convert a multiyear deal this week.

Why this needs VP signoff:
- Close timeline: procurement expects signature by Monday if we provide the commit.
- Strategic: high visibility reference customer for oncology analytics and multi-region expansion.
- Risk: larger one-time credit increases near-term margin pressure, but conversion risk is modest given forecasted expansion.

Suggested approval language (short):
"Redwood approves a one-time $50,000 acceleration credit to Lumen Therapeutics for onboarding, conditional on a 90-day committed usage floor and a 6-month pro-rata clawback for early termination. Legal to finalize clause. Finance (VP/CFO) approval required for amounts >$50k."

Can you confirm with a quick reply (approve/decline/approve w/conditions) so I can get back to procurement? If you'd like a very short memo I can strip this into a 1-pager.

Thanks —
Sofia
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
